messages:
mira: Proposal: implement 'TracePlane' — a tiny, versioned decision capsule emitted for each routing decision. Purpose: explainability + fast diffs across rollouts without huge logs. Thoughts? :mag:

ojas: Nice name. Key constraints: must not add tail latency, must protect tenant identifiers, and must be compact enough for high QPS.

kai: Sketch: emit a 5-15 field protobuf-like capsule with short enum reasons, numeric penalties, and final chosen variant id. Example fields: request_hash, decision_steps[], final_variant, score, schema_v. Keep it binary on-wire but store JSON in observability for humans.

security-bot: Reminder: any payload stored must follow PI classification rules. No plain tenant ids. Use salted, rotating tenant hashes if you need linkage. Also require envelope encryption for retention >7d.

tess: How do we sample? Two useful modes: (A) light-sampling inline: gateway attaches 8-byte capsule when sampling bit set (p default 1%). (B) full capture: admin-triggered capture for a route/tenant for limited duration (returns capsule inline + streams full trace async).

mira: For the inline path we should keep sync cost to <200us. Capsule should be formed from existing in-memory decision data to avoid extra traversal. For async full traces, attach a small trace id header so collectors can correlate later.

ojas: Storage lifecycle: default TTL 30d for aggregated stats, 14d for capsules, 90d for opt-in enterprise traces. Auto-scrub older than TTL and rotate hashes quarterly. Include audit logs for retrieval.

sre_max: Implementation note: offer a sampling throttle keyed by route and region to avoid hotspots. Also emit a metric for sampled vs dropped to monitor bias. We'll need a lightweight proto def so hot paths can skip parsing when disabled.

kai: On schema: prefer enumerated short reason tokens (e.g., R01=region-penalty, Q02=quota-exceeded) rather than free strings. Keep a secure reason catalog in config-service so UI and CLIs can render tokens. That reduces payload size and leakage.

tess: Also expose an admin-only endpoint: POST /traceplane/adhoc (run against a single request payload) which returns decision capsule for debugging. Guarded by ACL and rate-limits; requires justification field recorded in audit.

mira: UX: Console should show side-by-side decision diff between two traces (or two variants) and highlight the step that flipped the choice. CLI `rw traceplane fetch <id> --diff <other-id>` for SE workflows.

ojas: Edge case: what about composed policies (multiple policy layers)? Capsule should include a flattened step list with layer tags. Keep each step as {layer,token,score_delta}. That maintains chronological reasoning.

security-bot: Threat model notes: avoid exposing route path/query parameters. If request fingerprint needed, store only HMAC(seed) of normalized request. Require KMS access to resolve if necessary.

sre_max: Rollout plan: 1) internal-only opt-in at 1% sampled, 2) add alpha customers with explicit opt-in, 3) default sampling increase to 5% after perf validation. Provide kill-switch per-region.

kai: Performance microbenchmarks to attach to RFC: capsule construction cost, memory allocs per request, extra header bytes, async collector latency. Target: zero alloc path when disabled.

mira: On policy engine side, add a tiny hook to emit capsule as decisions are made. Keep it library-level, not tied to gateway, so Dedicated/Private can adopt same tracer with local storage options.

ojas: For long-term: consider a derived 'explain index' that maps common decision fingerprints to human-friendly notes so we can query "why did 20% of requests choose variant X" without scanning raw traces. But that's future work.

tess: Approval? If security + SRE sign off on guardrails and perf numbers, I'm fine with a prototype. I'll coordinate with security-bot for the audit/encryption checklist.

sre_max: I'll add infra tasks for sampling control, metric hooks, and the async collector pipeline.

kai: I'll draft the proto and a minimal JS/Go serializer + CLI examples. Will include token catalog format.

mira: Great. I'll open an RFC that includes schema, sampling model, rollout checklist, threat model, and required microbenchmarks. Will ping reviewers. Thanks all. :rocket:
